# Distill meeting notes: PostgreSQL & Slack

**Pattern:** AI Summarize & Route · **Level:** Advanced · **Trigger:** Webhook

## Overview

Fires when a webhook arrives, and covers knowledge-sync work end to end across PostgreSQL, Slack and Discord.

It moves through 17 working steps plus a 2-node error rail, in this order:

1. Receive Inbound Webhook
2. Read Recent from PostgreSQL
3. Newest First
4. Trim to Digest Size
5. Summarize Content (AI)
6. Groq Chat Model
7. Render as HTML
8. Post Digest to Discord
9. Post Digest to Slack
10. Confirm All Sends
11. Archive Digest in PostgreSQL
12. Guard Non-Empty title
13. Cap Batch Volume
14. Stamp Processing Time
15. Summarize Run Stats
16. Append Audit Row (PostgreSQL)
17. Send Summary to Discord

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing knowledge-sync work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Receive Inbound Webhook → Read Recent from PostgreSQL → Newest First → Trim to Digest Size → Summarize Content (AI) → Groq Chat Model → Render as HTML → Post Digest to Discord → Post Digest to Slack → Confirm All Sends → Archive Digest in PostgreSQL → Guard Non-Empty title → Cap Batch Volume → Stamp Processing Time → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (PostgreSQL) → Send Summary to Discord → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack

## Use it for

- Teams keeping PostgreSQL and Slack aligned by hand for knowledge sync
- Pushing knowledge-sync events into PostgreSQL and Slack the moment they land, not on the next poll
- Knowledge sync work where "Read Recent from PostgreSQL" is still a manual step before PostgreSQL
- Knowledge sync work that only reaches PostgreSQL when a webhook arrives, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps PostgreSQL and Slack in step for knowledge sync, without anyone re-typing a row
- A failed PostgreSQL or Slack call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 19 nodes in this knowledge-sync build
- Branches rejoin before PostgreSQL, so a knowledge-sync run reports once rather than 19 times
- The knowledge-sync AI step is isolated from PostgreSQL, so models swap without touching the other 19 nodes
- Fans the same result out to Discord in the same run, for knowledge sync

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Discord webhook URL; Groq API key; Postgres connection; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Summarization uses a Chain, not an Agent, because the step is fixed — there's no decision about which tool to call, just 'summarize this text.' Posting to multiple channels runs as parallel branches, not sequential sends, so a slow API on one channel never delays the message that was already ready on another.

## Practice exercises

You've got the basics covered — push further:

1. Add a third notification channel and watch the Merge node's input count update.
2. Change 'Trim to Digest Size' from 15 to 5 and see how it narrows the summary's scope.
3. Swap the Summarization Chain for a Q&A Chain to answer questions instead of just recapping.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Postgres connection**
Host, port, database, user, password from your Postgres provider.
_Gotcha:_ Managed providers usually require SSL enabled in the credential's options.

**Groq API key**
console.groq.com → API Keys.
_Gotcha:_ Very fast and cheap, but with tight per-minute rate limits.

**Discord webhook URL**
Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook → Copy URL.
_Gotcha:_ Webhook mode needs no bot token. Messages cap at 2000 characters.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**Webhook returns 404**
Cause: Calling the test URL when the workflow is published, or vice versa.
Fix: Test URL works only while 'Listen for test event' is armed; the production URL needs the workflow published.

**AI node fails with an auth or quota error**
Cause: API key missing billing, or the per-minute rate limit was hit.
Fix: Confirm the provider account has credit. For rate limits, lower concurrency or switch to a higher-quota model.

**The AI returns the wrong shape or rambles**
Cause: The prompt is under-specified for the task.
Fix: Tighten the System Message: state the role, the constraints, and the exact output format you expect.

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

**Database node cannot connect**
Cause: SSL not enabled, or the n8n server's IP is not allow-listed.
Fix: Most managed database providers require both.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- PostgreSQL: connect as a role that can reach only the tables below, not as the owner.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.
- Discord: give the bot access to the destination channel only, not the whole guild.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole knowledge-sync payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.

The webhook path is unguessable but it is not authentication: add header auth or an IP allow-list before this endpoint is reachable from the internet.

## 🤖 AI cluster

Purple nodes form one AI unit: the root node orchestrates, sub-nodes plug in via typed ports (model / memory / tools / parser). Swap the chat model without rewiring anything else. Costs scale with tokens — keep prompts lean and cap iterations.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your knowledge sync process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.
